summary: PASS 38 / FAIL 2 / NOT_VERIFIABLE_OFFLINE 18 / N/A 0. Verdict: every (role, holder) pair that 02 §9.2 prescribes for DataStore (32 pairs: 16 CONTROLLER, 4 ROUTER_PLUGIN, 2 each CONFIG/LIMITED_CONFIG/MARKET_KEEPER, 1 each ORDER/FROZEN_ORDER/LIQUIDATION/ADL/FEE_KEEPER/TIMELOCK_ADMIN) is present on-chain at block 46282993, role hashes match Role.sol, the bootstrap deployer 0x4b32f9bc... retains exactly the §9.3-listed DataStore roles (DEFAULT_ADMIN, CONTROLLER, CONFIG_KEEPER, LIMITED_CONFIG_KEEPER, MARKET_KEEPER) and nothing more, and §18.1 `hasRole(CONTROLLER, OrderHandler)` = true with no v0.3.1 address holding any role. The two FAIL rows are the same finding: DataStore CONTROLLER has one extra member, the E2E admin EOA 0xf82cf35c5c0019861c2cdc65041c8ac32970d403, which is not the bootstrap deployer (so §9.3 does not explain it) but is an intentional TestCode harness grant (deploy-contracts.ts:43/657, roles.json.grants[4]) that the 02 manual does not document. LPVault CONTROLLER_ROLE, Treasury x2 roles and ReferralStorage handlers (17 pairs) plus LPVault/Treasury DEFAULT_ADMIN and ProxyAdmin ownership are outside the offline snapshot; the r3 ignition journal shows all 17 corresponding grant/setHandler transactions confirmed SUCCESS before the snapshot block, but that is deploy-time evidence, not a read-back.
caveats: Extra CONTROLLER on 0xf82cf35c... is explained (TestCode/scripts/deploy-contracts.ts step 8, line 657; roles.json.grants[4]; manifest .roles.controller) but is a real deviation from 02 §9.2 and is a powerful right (direct DataStore writes); acceptable only as a fork-only harness convenience. Recommend either documenting it in 02 §9.2/§18.1 (or CURRENT.json) as a known test-environment grant, or revoking it after configure so the fork mirrors the manual.

In the tx-fork parameter file the multisig, feeKeeper, configKeeper, limitedConfigKeeper, marketKeeper and timelockAdmin are all the same EOA 0xf82CF35C... and orderKeeper/liquidationKeeper/adlKeeper are all 0x542fe841... (fx100.fork.tx-fork.json). The §9.2 fallback-to-deployer rule (02:250) did not trigger (no zero addresses), but privilege concentration on two EOAs is test-only and must not be copied to production.

parameters.json .roles[] enumerates only the 11 DataStore roles; DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is known only through roles.json.defaultAdminRoleMember0 (member index 0). Additional DEFAULT_ADMIN members, if any, cannot be excluded offline.

LPVault / ProtocolTreasury / InsuranceTreasury / ReferralStorage role state is not captured by config-dump; the 17 NOT_VERIFIABLE_OFFLINE rows rely on ignition journal receipts (status SUCCESS, blocks 46282751-46282873, all before snapshot block 46282993). Suggest extending config-dump (or the deploy read-back step 9) to read LPVault.hasRole(CONTROLLER_ROLE,x), Treasury.hasRole(...), ReferralStorage.isHandler(x) so these become chain-verified.

The §18.1 clause 'old address (in-place upgrade) = false' is trivially satisfied: tx-fork v0.3.2 is a fresh deployment with a new DataStore (0x4741A9C9...), not an in-place upgrade of the v0.3.1 DataStore (0x606D72Ab...). The check confirms none of the 22 v0.3.1 addresses hold any role on the new DataStore.

parameters-by-module.csv was not consulted; role data lives in parameters.json .roles[], which was used directly. Address mapping snapshot deployed-addresses.json is identical (67 keys, 0 diffs) to ignition deployed_addresses.json for tx-fork-v032-260902r3 and consistent with the manifest.

Per ground rules no .env*, pk.txt, mnemonic, noise-traders.json, Devconfig/ or Memory/ files were read; TestCode/config/environments/tx-fork-260729.json matched the address grep but was deliberately not opened (environment files may carry RPC URLs). The manifest, parameter file and CURRENT.json were read through a redaction filter and contained no URL/secret. E2E_ADMIN_ACCOUNT / E2E_KEEPER_ACCOUNT values were not read; their on-chain effect is taken from the ignition parameter file and the snapshot.
Older ignition deployment ids tx-fork-v032-260901 and tx-fork-v032-260902 (non-r3) also exist in the contract clone; they are separate deployments and were not used for any actual value here.
